notes.fact: Russia and Ukraine agreed in principle to a large prisoner exchange after two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, with no breakthrough on ceasefire or territory.
notes.event: Abu Dhabi talks end with prisoner swap

notes.fact: AP reports both sides confirmed a large POW exchange and that hopes for any significant development had been low before the first meeting in nine months.
notes.event: Abu Dhabi talks end with prisoner swap

notes.fact: Russia's state-funded RT says talks centred on European security architecture and that Western European envoys were sidelined; it reports the swap could come in two to three weeks.
notes.event: Abu Dhabi talks end with prisoner swap

notes.fact: Russia's Medinsky said the sides had moved closer to peace but that much depends on Ukraine, the US and Europe; the Moscow Times says neither side has shown major compromise.
notes.event: Abu Dhabi talks end with prisoner swap

notes.fact: Putin aide Ushakov confirmed the Thursday meeting and said the Americans were bringing something; Meduza says participants voiced cautious optimism.
India's Tribune (ANI) cites CNN that Trump's recent concessions to Moscow worry European capitals, and that Moscow has resisted a multilateral format including Europe.
After a Russian drone attack on Kryvyi Rih infrastructure, part of the city was still without power on Nov 11; some hospitals and water pumps ran on generators, city defence council head said.
Zelensky said Ukrainian forces again face systematic limits on Starshield satellite internet, making it harder to intercept Russian jet drones; Musk denied deliberately throttling it.
Kyiv hoped Abu Dhabi would advance a ceasefire covering Black Sea grain shipments; Foreign Minister Sybiha said Ukraine was still awaiting Moscow's response.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy says two supertankers were disabled by explosions on Nov 11 night after using an unauthorised route; Iranian state media says they hit mines.
Xinhua carried the IRGC statement that two tankers were disabled by blasts after ignoring warnings; it gave no independent confirmation of ships or damage.
Kenyan outlet Streamline, citing AFP and Reuters, says the claim is unconfirmed: UKMTO's latest entries (Nov 10) match neither ship, and the US military recently said all mines were cleared.
Reuters, via Ynet, reported attackers on a small boat attached limpet mines to the Panama-flagged tanker Louise 1 near Khasab; no crew were hurt and it resumed its voyage.
Iran's security chief Rezaei told Al Mayadeen that Iran would strike US bases, including in Europe, if aircraft from them bomb Iran.
notes.event: Rezaei threat to US bases in Europe

notes.fact: Pakistan's Daily Times, citing Press TV, says Rezaei named no bases or countries and claimed Iran's capabilities exceed those on the first day of the war.
notes.event: Rezaei threat to US bases in Europe

notes.fact: Arab News says Rezaei denied any talks with Washington and that his remarks followed US officials downplaying new strikes; it notes Trump's softer tone since the Nov 3 midterms.
notes.event: Rezaei threat to US bases in Europe

notes.fact: Aggregator Newscord, summarising Times of Israel and others, says Rezaei set seven conditions for reopening Hormuz and called reports of Qatari-mediation progress false.
CBS's live page lists headlines that the US moved aircraft from a second UK base over a reported Iran threat and that a counter-terror probe followed an RAF Fairford incident.
Spectrum News cites the Pentagon's casualty system: 23 US service members have died and at least 865 been wounded in the Iran war; Trump cited 18 dead.
Al Jazeera's live blog says Israel ordered its military to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran; it does not say who reported this or give a source.
The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed five missiles and two drones fired by Houthis at Saudi Arabia on Nov 11, including three cruise missiles aimed at the Riyadh region.
notes.event: Houthi missiles at Saudi Arabia and Aden

notes.fact: Dawn, citing AFP, says the UN counts over 1,600 killed and 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed in summer; 26 people died in Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia.
notes.event: Houthi missiles at Saudi Arabia and Aden

notes.fact: Middle East Eye reported the coalition said it destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at western Saudi Arabia; the Houthis deny targeting Mecca, per the coalition's earlier statement account.
notes.event: Houthi missiles at Saudi Arabia and Aden

notes.fact: An Israeli air strike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis killed six, including a surgeon, and wounded 12 to 20, Gaza health and civil defence officials said.
The Israeli military said it hit a senior Hamas member using the hospital as a command centre, without public evidence; Hamas denied any fighters were inside.
Al Jazeera says seven others were killed across Gaza before the hospital strike and over 1,600 Palestinians died since the October 2025 ceasefire, per Gaza's health ministry.
AP via KSAT says Israel controls at least 60% of Gaza and that 1,622 people were killed since the truce began, per health authorities.
AFRICOM announced an airstrike on al-Shabaab near Jamaame on Nov 5, coordinated with Somalia's government; it gave no casualty details.
Somali media cite local security sources saying US aircraft struck ISIS positions in Puntland's Qandala district on Nov 9; AFRICOM has not confirmed it.
FDD says US troops left Baledogle airfield but strikes continue; the New York Sun says AFRICOM's Nov 5 strike was the 91st of 2026.
New America counts about 5.4 US strikes a month from June to October versus 12.6 a month January-May; none declared against ISIS-Somalia since May 6.

CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT published a fact sheet warning that attackers target industrial refrigeration and cold-chain controllers; the same equipment is used in US grocery, health and food sectors.
BleepingComputer reports 250-350 French supermarkets were hit in October, then a second wave hit over 115 stores in six European countries; French blood facilities saw altered temperatures on Nov 3.

SC World, citing Nextgov-linked reporting, says up to six US military commissaries had refrigeration failures since late August; a link to European attacks is unproven and Iran-linked suspicion is unattributed.

Science Times reports attacks on US water systems across at least 12 states; the FBI says attackers changed settings on internet-facing PLCs, officials call Iran a suspect, not confirmed, with no widespread supply loss.
